This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via environmentId (literal, a string literal in deleteMetaItemUnaudited))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via environmentId (literal, a string literal in deleteMetaItemUnaudited))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7af31ee30bd0a5bd032a800a43489dacacabc0cb` — the merge of head `d311b66322543204efbd2f4526559ffcae4bebb7` into base `bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7af31ee30bd0a5bd032a800a43489dacacabc0cb && git checkout 7af31ee30bd0a5bd032a800a43489dacacabc0cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947 d311b66322543204efbd2f4526559ffcae4bebb7 && git checkout -B drift-repro bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947 && git merge --no-ff d311b66322543204efbd2f4526559ffcae4bebb7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bf02d33bd64f496aa8166e1a235ef10977927947` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c35a911b3073eafa6d152e2101a566322cd5c4a0`
Local-runs: none

First round on the declaration face (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`; no published schema, no governed path, no narrowing arm), read at 2026-11-13T16:42Z. Inputs: card #32552, the PR body, the diff against merge base `2c98485d` (five files), the check-runs on this head, the knock 6858183179. Claim 6858479168. Read for the judgments below, not reviewed as a design: `someShipperOf` and its three call sites, and the `[#32552]` pins.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. Two doors admit a request they refused: the removal naming the second holder's pair goes from `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` to `200`, and a commit revert into that pair goes from `failed[]` to restored. Nothing that was admitted is refused.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write is added, refused or given a new meaning.
- The one-holder answer does not move. `someShipperOf` asks the bare-name owner first, and with one shipper the set it walks next holds that same package.
- No shipper is picked. Each call judges the row or the pair the request itself names, and asks only whether it is a pair of some package that ships the name. A pair of no shipper keeps its `403` and stays in the census (pinned in both orders).
- The census row is true on this base for a flow only (s1).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` follows from `none`. A widening carries no BREAKING banner and no `!`, and none is written. No ADR-0087 marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 51 runs, 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed.
- Order. The card and the PR put this after #32613, whose PR #33126 holds FAIL 6858448985 on `c0b7cb13`. This head's base does not carry that fix. The trial merge against it is named in the PR as the seat's step before queueing; both PRs add a describe to `packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts`.
- The census overlaps #32859, as the PR says. The seat's.
- The full dogfood battery was still running when the PR opened; its line goes to the os-dev report on the card. Not owed by the declaration (no `!`, no narrowing arm). Not read here.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is reported NOT MEASURED locally and left to CI.
- 92 commits on the branch, from the earlier branches it resumes; the diff against `main` is the five files.

Findings:

- **s1 should-fix. The census sentence is true for a flow on this base, and for the other sealed types only after #33126.** Derived from the code, not run. The census now leaves out a row that is the declared override of any shipper, for every type. On `main` the reads serve a second holder's declared override for a flow (every shipper since #31696), but for an action, a page, an app, a dataset, a doc, a book and a mapping they still judge the row against the first-registered holder and decline it; #33126 is the change that moves them. So landed ahead of #33126, the census would stop naming a second holder's action override that the reads do not serve, which is the opposite of what the table's "live declared override" says. The census pin here boots both holders with a flow and an action override and expects an empty census, so it holds that silence too. Owed: land after #33126, as planned, and keep the census in step with whatever #33126 ends up serving (its M1 may leave the six sealed types on the first-holder judgment, and then the census must keep naming them); say in the table that the census row is the flow's on `main` and the action's with #32613.
- **n1 nit.** "any open override type" on the removal row: the pins remove a flow, and an action in the condition-1 probe. The revert and the census are pinned on a flow.

No must-fix.

Claim 6862544400. `protocol-environment-rows.ts` and `protocol-class-head.ts` are unchanged since `c35a911b`, and what the earlier record judged in them stands as read there.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand. The commit takes a widening back for six types and adds none: the census moves for a flow and an action only.
- The census now asks the question the reads ask. For a flow and an action it judges the row against every shipper, as `declinesStoredRow` does since #33126. For any other type it is the expression `main` has, the name's first-registered shipper alone, so nothing moves there.
- The removal and the revert still judge every shipper for every type. That is consistent with the census: for a sealed type the second holder's override is a row the reads decline and the census names for deletion, and the removal that deletes it is now admitted where it was refused.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, no BREAKING banner, no `!`, no ADR-0087 marker: unchanged, and right for a widening of kind `none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 55 runs, 37 success, 18 skipped, none failed. The eight `Test Core` shards, the type checks and `Check Changeset` are green.
- Order. #33126 and #33130 are on `main` and in this head; the merge base is `bf02d33b`, and `main` is two commits past it, none on a path of this diff. Both PRs added a describe to `packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts`; the merge kept both, and the file's run in CI is the reading of that.
- The census overlaps #32859, as the PR says. The seat's.
- The full dogfood battery was read on `c35a911b` and not re-run for this delta; not owed by the declaration (no `!`, no narrowing arm). The ablation legs and local runs are the report's; none was run here.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` (s1). Fixed. `perShipperType` is `flow` or `action` by the canonical type; the two arms share one predicate call, so only the base it is judged against differs. The comment says why and names the card that moves the six. The new CONTROL boots two holders that each ship a mapping, stores each holder's declared mapping override, and expects the census to name exactly one row in both registration orders. By the report's ablation it goes red when the type restriction is removed, so it holds the line s1 asked for.

`.changeset/32552-pair-row-removal-every-shipper.md` and the PR table (s1, n1). The census row reads "a flow or an action only", a paragraph says what the six sealed types keep and until when, and each row names what it is pinned on.

Findings:

- None on this delta.

No must-fix. s1 and n1 of record 6859128505 are closed on this head. The census line carries a type and a name and no package, so `mapping×1` over two stored rows is as far as the CONTROL can pin which row is named.
